findings.text: Record text formatting clamps the stored length to the available buffer capacity, derives a single line prefix from metadata and mode flags, then walks newline separated lines prepending that prefix to each line in place by shifting the tail and inserting the prefix, ensures the final line ends with a newline, drops whole lines when capacity is insufficient and discards truncated tail, always terminates the buffer when its size is positive, and reports the prepared byte count excluding the terminator.

Prefix construction emits an optional system log tag followed by an optional timestamp followed by an optional caller tag, then appends a blank separator and termination when caller detail is enabled or timestamps are requested, returning the total prefix length.

Caller rendering has two build variants: one formats the numeric identity with a leading letter that distinguishes whether the high flag bit is set, enclosed in fixed width brackets, while the other variant produces no output and reports zero length.

Execution context loading has two build variants: one resolves processor number and process identifier from record metadata through dedicated helpers and copies the command name with a compile time size equality check, while the other variant does nothing.

Process and processor derivation selects between two stored caller fields based on a mask flag in the first field, returning the appropriate field for process identity and the masked counterpart for processor number with the flag bit removed.
A read handle for ring records holds a pointer to metadata storage plus a pointer to text storage and the text capacity, all installed by a small initializer.

Default console priority prefers panic when the current processor is panicking, else emergency when the per processor emergency nesting counter is nonzero, else normal; a disabled build variant always reports none.

Emergency nesting state is addressed through an early global counter before per processor print data is ready and through a per processor counter afterwards; readiness itself is reported by a global flag in one build and as always false in a minimal build.
Unsafe console takeover is permitted only when the current processor is panicking and a global panic takeover allowance is also enabled.

Next reservation sequence is derived from the last finalized sequence plus the distance between head identifier and last finalized identifier plus one, loading the finalized sequence before the head identifier for ordering, retrying when the finalized record was overwritten, and handling the never finalized case with a special initial identifier check that yields zero or anchors from the first descriptor.

Descriptor validation distinguishes missing versus lost data versus usable: identifier miss, reserved or committed state, or sequence mismatch means absent; reusable state or doubly failed block pointers means present but data lost; otherwise the descriptor is accepted as finalized.

Panic console flushing ignores locking, clears the flag that would allow scheduling, optionally rewinds all consoles for full replay, triggers nonblocking atomic flush when the selected flush type requests it, and then flushes legacy consoles whenever panic synchronization for them is allowed even if unsafe.

Flush method selection depends on default priority and console population and block conditions: normal prefers offload threads when running and unblocked else atomic or direct paths, emergency prefers atomic or direct, panic never offloads and suppresses legacy direct output while atomic nonblocking output is active unless legacy panic sync is allowed, warning on unknown priority and treating legacy deferral as false in the minimal build.

Atomic pending flush walks consoles under read side protection, skips consoles lacking the nonblocking flag or unusable or already caught up, flushes each lagging console toward a stop sequence, and for a single console repeats with a refreshed stop sequence when flushing succeeded but more valid records appeared and offload is unavailable, stopping promptly on new ownership or on records not yet finalized.

Validity probing loops on read errors by catching up to the first available sequence when behind the tail, skipping one sequence when data was lost, and otherwise failing except that the panicking processor may skip over non finalized entries when further reservations exist and either non panic debugging is disabled or legacy panic sync is allowed.

Record reading resolves the descriptor identifier for the requested sequence, validates that it is finalized for that sequence, treats a null record as an existence probe, otherwise copies metadata when requested and copies text through the data ring with failure reported as lost data, then revalidates that the sequence is still finalized.

Data copying succeeds immediately when neither buffer nor line count is requested, otherwise resolves the block and fails when unresolvable or when the stored extent is smaller than expected, optionally reports line count, and copies at most the smaller of buffer capacity and expected length.

Block resolution treats doubly dataless empty line markers as successful empty content and other dataless markers as failure, accepts either non wrapping extents or extents wrapping once with the start one ring behind the end, maps the start to a block address, validates alignment and minimum payload beyond the identifier and maximum size, and warns on illegal descriptions.

Data ring helpers derive total size from a size bit count, derive an index by masking a logical position, derive a block address from a masked offset into the data array, test dataless by requiring both endpoints to be dataless, and accept zero size or block sizes fitting within half the ring.

Console iteration uses a nonmaskable interrupt safe sleepable read lock with cookie based release, held across the atomic flush walk; sequence computation relies on acquire ordering between the last finalized load and the head identifier load pairing with release ordering in the reservation path, plus an acquire load when reading the last finalized sequence.

In place prefix expansion can drop trailing lines under capacity pressure and can iterate once with zero remaining bytes to emit an empty prefixed line; termination is guaranteed only when capacity is positive and the terminator is excluded from the reported length.

Racy reads of expected length, descriptor state, and finalized sequence can observe torn or overwritten values and are contained by size checks, post copy revalidation, retry on overwrite, catch up to the tail, and by never waiting for non finalized records during atomic flush to avoid deadlock; panic flushing deliberately bypasses locks and may emit even when unsafe.
System log priority value combines facility shifted left by three positions with level, rendered as decimal digits inside angle brackets.
Timestamp rendering splits a nanosecond count using a divisor of one billion into seconds and remaining nanoseconds, displaying seconds and microseconds in fixed width decimal fields inside brackets.

Caller identity uses the top bit as a thread versus processor selector with the remaining bits as numeric identity, rendered with a leading letter distinguishing the selector inside fixed width brackets.
Kernel debugger state clearing removes the selected named flag from a global state word.

Record validity probing has two providers: one header defines it as constantly false for a disabled configuration, while the ring implementation performs a real skip aware validity walk; callers in the disabled case never observe valid records.

Globally visible services in this lane are default priority query, unsafe takeover check, next reservation sequence query, console read lock and unlock, panic flush, atomic pending flush, per processor readiness query, and record validity probe.
